transcript.content: Hi, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

I know a few people in my department have quietly agreed to block my grants and promotions, and I can’t shake that belief no matter how much my wife or colleagues argue with me. My wife actually insisted I come in to talk to someone, but I just can't ignore what is happening.

How long have you been convinced that people in your department are blocking your grants and promotions? Did this belief start suddenly over days to weeks, or has it been building and lasting for months or longer?

This has been going on for about a year now, and it definitely didn't happen overnight. It built up gradually after I lost a major research grant for the second time and a younger colleague got a faculty position. Over the months, my frustration turned into a firm conviction as I started noticing subtle signs, like delayed emails and sudden changes to meeting agendas.
Aside from this belief about your colleagues, have you had experiences like hearing voices when no one is there, or have others said your speech or behavior has become noticeably disorganized or odd?

No, I’ve never heard any voices or had hallucinations, and no one has accused me of acting or speaking strangely. Aside from the stress of dealing with my colleagues, my day-to-day life is completely normal; I still teach my classes, grade papers on time, and handle everything at home just fine.

During this past year, have you had long periods of feeling unusually depressed or unusually energized with much less need for sleep? If so, did those mood changes happen at the same time as your belief about your colleagues?

No, I haven't experienced those kinds of extreme mood swings—neither feeling deeply depressed nor unusually energized with less need for sleep. My mood has been relatively normal, apart from the obvious frustration and stress related to my situation at work.
What makes you certain your colleagues are blocking your grants and promotions—have you seen direct proof, or is it mainly based on patterns like delayed emails and meeting changes?

While others might dismiss these things as coincidences, to me, the delayed emails, sudden meeting changes, and lukewarm feedback on my teaching form a clear, undeniable pattern. I've spent long evenings analyzing committee rosters and funding announcements, which has only solidified my certainty that they are actively coordinating to sideline me.

Has anyone ever directly told you they were trying to block your grants or promotion, or is your belief based entirely on patterns you’ve noticed? Even when presented with clear evidence against it, do you still feel completely certain it’s true?

No, no one has directly admitted it to me, but the patterns like delayed emails, lukewarm teaching feedback, and sudden agenda changes are just too consistent to be coincidences. Even though my wife and colleagues constantly argue with me and try to prove otherwise, I remain absolutely certain that this small group is actively working to stall my career.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a single, persistent persecutory delusion lasting about one year, held with firm conviction despite contrary evidence. There are no hallucinations, no disorganized speech or behavior, no prominent negative symptoms, and no sustained depressive or manic episodes. Functioning is largely preserved outside the delusional theme, supporting persistent delusional disorder rather than schizophrenia or a mood disorder with psychotic features.
